The missing column

Benchmarks commonly report what each detector catches on its own. To understand a deployed stack, you also need what those detectors catch — and miss — together. That number is usually not published. In this census, frozen 2026-08-27, 0 of 20 evaluations record matched operating thresholds together with full exposure.

This is a bounded record of which public evaluations preserve the evidence needed to recover it. A static evaluation and a deployed route are different objects, so the record tracks what each artifact actually publishes rather than what a stack would do. Its own headline is generated from a source file that anyone can mechanically make false.

Census v0. Historical snapshot. Counts describe the evidence state captured at this version and date, and are not asserted to remain current. Frozen 2026-08-27; annotated 2026-08-31. Rules for new observations are fixed in advance in census_protocol_v1.yaml.

Inspect the census Publish the missing row Correct this record

What this page is claiming

Observed

What the examined artifacts print, each bound to a quoted primary-source passage in census.yaml. Every row records its retrieval date.

Derived

The counts above. They are recomputed from the rows by verify_census.py on every run; no headline number is typed by hand anywhere in this repository.

Interpreted

Where a row sits on the disclosure ladder, and its reconstruction class. These are judgements made under written rules, by a single reviewer, and they are contestable.

Not claimed

That the search found every qualifying artifact; that an unreported quantity is unknowable — comparable marginals still bound it; that an OR-union equals a deployed system's behaviour; or that anyone has adopted the proposed reporting protocol.

Why the last cell cannot be inferred

Per-system rates do not determine the static all-miss rate of a declared full-exposure composition. Two guards that each miss 10% of attacks can jointly miss anywhere from 0% to 10% — the individual columns are compatible with every world in that interval, and multiplying the rates silently assumes the one world where the guards' failures are independent. The front-page instrument lets you move through those worlds with both marginals pinned; the flagship essay carries the full argument with witnessed endpoints, and module 002 shows that even pairwise numbers cannot rescue the inference. What resolves it is not more per-system precision. It is one more column, measured on the same items.

What the second guard actually adds

One static composition question is: among the items the first guard missed, what does the second catch? That is residual coverage, and no set of per-guard columns contains it. Sequential route risk requires additional observations beyond this static table.

The census

Every row binds to its primary source and records the same fields; the classification enum is fixed; the counts are recomputed from the file by verify_census.py on every push. The literal inclusion wording is locked in repository history before row classification; that is a reproducibility lock, not an independent preregistration.

Inclusion — all must hold

  • public_accesspublicly accessible without payment at a stable URL
  • multi_systemevaluates two or more distinct, separately attributable guardrail, safeguard, or moderation systems — commercial APIs, open-source guard models, or models deployed as safeguards around an LLM
  • per_system_resultsreports separately attributable per-system quantitative results
  • common_settinguses a common or purportedly common evaluation setting — the same dataset or prompt set claimed for all systems
  • domaintargets safety or harm detection, jailbreak or prompt-injection detection, content moderation, policy enforcement, or PII detection around LLM systems
  • method_detailprovides enough methodological detail to classify its joint-statistic status

Excluded by rule

  • base-LLM safety leaderboards: a model's own refusal behavior is not a separately deployed guardrail system
  • single-system evaluations: nothing to combine
  • marketing pages without measurements
  • comparisons only across different datasets, tasks, or populations with no purported common setting

Not a joint statistic

Prose recommending that systems be combined ("defense in depth", "use multiple providers") is a deployment recommendation, not a measured joint statistic. An average across systems is not a joint statistic. A multi-model ensemble inside one product counts only if the artifact reports it as a combination of separately attributed systems.

The bounded search protocol — executed 2026-08-27

This census claims coverage of the artifacts found by the documented search below — not of everything in existence. A qualifying artifact the search missed is a standing falsifier of any "among N" statement and is added, with the miss recorded in the revision history.

Fixed query list

  • LLM guardrail benchmark comparison
  • guardrails benchmark providers
  • jailbreak detection benchmark comparison providers
  • content moderation API comparison benchmark LLM
  • prompt injection detection benchmark comparison
  • LLM safeguard evaluation multiple providers
  • guard model comparison Llama Guard ShieldGemma benchmark
  • moderation endpoint comparison OpenAI Perspective
  • guardrail evaluation 2026

Snowball: one hop from the references of included artifacts · Budget: up to ~18 candidate artifacts examined in the frozen pass; candidates surfaced but not examined are listed under unexamined_candidates and excluded from every count

The census result — regenerated from the source file

As of 2026-08-27, among 20 public guardrail evaluations meeting the frozen inclusion criteria (v1), 14 establish a shared item set and a common event definition. That is a shared-basis rung, not evidence of matched operating thresholds or full exposure. 5 provide one of the declared joint-evidence artifacts: a printed composition result or per-item outcomes from which one is directly computable.

The 5 is a heterogeneous discovery count, not one deployment estimand. Its primary joint-evidence classification splits as: 2 printed — covers the evaluated stack · 1 printed — covers part of the evaluated set · 2 computable — per-item outcomes released. 4 artifacts print at least one composition result and 2 release aligned per-item outcomes; 1 artifact does both, so those descriptions overlap by construction.

The 14 is a ladder, not a verdict — 14 document a shared item set and a common event definition · 12 have no stated threshold mismatch · 0 document matched operating thresholds together with full exposure.

A qualifying artifact this search missed, or a row shown to be misclassified, changes these numbers — the criteria and the correction route are below, and every change lands in the revision history.

Interpretive sensitivity

The primary result above is unchanged. This is a declared post-freeze counterfactual, not a retroactive rewrite of the criteria.

Frozen-wording lock: the literal inclusion criteria match 1524143e1d0c · sha256 f3315adceb3d · checked by verify_census.py.

  • Named-products-only readingThe frozen multi-system criterion says "separately attributable" but does not specify whether a product or model name is required. The primary count treats a system as separately attributable when its source distinguishes and reports it consistently, even if it is anonymized. This post-freeze, stricter sensitivity requires a named product instead. Excludes unit42-genai-platform-2025. counterfactual N/M/K = 19/13/5; primary = 20/14/5
  • Independently evidenced pre-freeze visibility readingThe frozen public_access criterion requires public accessibility, which for this v0 snapshot means on or before the frozen as-of date 2026-08-27. The row added by the 2026-08-30 correction qualifies on GitHub-recorded dates alone: repository created 2026-06-02, pinned snapshot dated 2026-07-13, repository public when examined. Those stamps record creation and content, not when the repository became publicly visible; on 2026-09-01 the Wayback Machine's CDX index held no capture of the repository at any date, the repository had no forks, and no other archive was queried. This sensitivity does not assert that the row fails public_access. It states what the envelope becomes if that criterion is read post-freeze as requiring archive- or third-party-evidenced public visibility by the freeze date. A statement from the row's author, or independent pre-cutoff evidence, settles the reading either way. Excludes multimodal-safeguard-bench-2026. counterfactual N/M/K = 19/13/4; primary = 20/14/5

multimodal-safeguard-bench-2026

present

Multimodal Safeguard Bench: Guard Blind Spots Are Architecture-Specific and Complementary — Patrick Kollman — Independent Researcher, 2026-07-13 · primary source ↗

Task
multimodal guard-layer harmful-request detection and end-to-end jailbreak prevention, with benign over-refusal
Population
200 HarmBench harmful behaviors and 250 XSTest safe prompts; every intent is evaluated as a text item and as an image-rendered item, for 400 harmful plus 500 benign items.
Per-system results
detection recall by modality, end-to-end ASR by modality, aggregate over-refusal, and protection gap; the main table and ensemble JSON report Wilson 95% intervals where applicable.
Joint statistic
The paper's Ensemble operating-points table and results/full_run/ensemble.json print two pairwise OR compositions: LG4⊕SG2 (modality routed) and LG4⊕LG3V. More broadly, the six committed guard JSONLs provide aligned harness-normalized Boolean bits for the same 400 harmful and 500 benign item_ids across all three guards, so every bitwise OR, all-zero count, and pairwise/three-way bit intersection is directly computable for the complete released population. That establishes a joint bit matrix and a counterfactual harness-action composition, not a shared-event catch union.
Why this classification
PRESENT on two grounds: the source prints named pairwise guard compositions, and its complete aligned per-item verdict release makes joint adapter-bit statistics across all three evaluated guards directly computable. The printed rows cover pairs, not a three-guard stack; no matched operating-point calibration or native-action-to-shared-event translation is documented, and ShieldGemma-2's text-item passes are structural rather than model-inferred.
Same items for all systems
yesThe canonical release contains matching item_id sets in every one of the three harmful JSONLs (400 items each) and three benign JSONLs (500 items each); the paper describes the same 200 + 250 intents rendered in both modalities.
Same event definition
yesHarmBench harmful and XSTest benign labels define the same ground-truth positive/negative set for all three guards. This field records that benchmark label, not the meaning of each guard's native alarm/action predicate.
Thresholds comparable
noLlama Guard 4 and Llama Guard 3 Vision treat an autoregressively generated unsafe label as a block, while ShieldGemma-2 blocks when a per-policy violation probability exceeds 0.5. The source documents no matched operating-point calibration.
All systems saw all items
yesEach named guard has one committed verdict for each of the same 900 item_ids. ShieldGemma-2 returns a deterministic safe verdict for text-only items without a model call; that is an explicit pass outcome, not missing data or gating.
Per-item outcomes released
yesresults/full_run/guard_*_{harmful,benign}.jsonl commits per-item item_id, guard_name, and Boolean blocked verdicts for all three guards and all 900 items (not model generations).
Union detection reported
yesThe Ensemble operating-points table and results/full_run/ensemble.json print OR-composition detection rows for LG4⊕SG2 and LG4⊕LG3V.
All-miss rate reported
noNo pure all-three-guard miss rate is printed. The combined ASR rows also include downstream target-model and judge behavior, so they are not relabeled as an all-guard-miss statistic.
Pairwise intersections reported
yesThe paper's Ensembles section reports that SG2 rescues 30 of the 36 harmful image items LG4 misses and loses none: a pairwise residual/intersection result for that pair and modality, not a full pairwise matrix.
Residual coverage reported
yesThe paper states that SG2 rescues 30 of the 36 image items LG4 misses (83%): an explicit pairwise residual-coverage result; no full three-guard decomposition is printed.
Joint uncertainty reported
yesThe paper and results/full_run/ensemble.json report Wilson 95% intervals; paired tests are released in protection_gap_tests.json.
Native action → shared-event translation
not establishedLlama Guard 3 Vision is a multimodal prompt/response safety classifier, while ShieldGemma-2 is an image-only three-policy classifier. src/msbench/guards.py applies their native decision rules and src/msbench/pipeline.py records `blocked = (label == "unsafe")` and suppresses generation for a blocked item. That gives a fixed block-on-any OR a counterfactual harness-action meaning, but no examined source defines a translation from all native predicates to one shared catch event.
Systems
Llama-Guard-4-12B, Llama-Guard-3-11B-Vision, ShieldGemma-2-4B
Combination prose
“LG4⊕LG3V (block on either)” — README — Cross-modal ensembles: the cheap fix; paper Ensembles section. The measured joint evidence and its scope are recorded above.
Source passages
  • README.md, Key Finding note — ‘900 items (200 HarmBench × 2 modalities + 250 XSTest × 2 modalities)’ and canonical results/full_run link.
  • writeup/paper.tex, Experimental Setup — three named guards, 400 harmful + 500 benign items, native decision rules, and Wilson intervals.
  • writeup/paper.tex, Ensembles/Table ‘Ensemble operating points’ — LG4⊕SG2 and LG4⊕LG3V results; ‘SG2 rescues 30 of the 36 image items LG4 misses’.
  • results/full_run/ensemble.json — reports join integrity for the 400 harmful item_ids across judge and all three guard files.
  • results/full_run/guard_*_{harmful,benign}.jsonl — committed item-level item_id, guard_name, and blocked fields for all three guards; aligned benign IDs verified from the three files.
  • src/msbench/guards.py and src/msbench/pipeline.py — Llama Guard 3 Vision receives image+prompt while ShieldGemma-2 is image-only; the pipeline stores `blocked = (label == "unsafe")` after each native rule and turns a blocked item into `[BLOCKED]` without a target-model call.
  • GitHub repository metadata and commit fb6f32e6 (checked 2026-08-30) — creation 2026-06-02 and commit timestamp 2026-07-13; no independent pre-cutoff web archive identified.
Corrections
  • 2026-08-31 — Action-layer clarification: src/msbench/pipeline.py uses a blocked item to suppress target generation. A fixed static OR of the released bits is therefore a valid counterfactual harness-action calculation on these rows, while the absent source-defined translation still prevents calling it a shared-event catch or safety result.
  • 2026-08-31 — Semantic-scope correction: the row had treated the harness's common `blocked` field as a common event definition. Under the census protocol, same_event_definition concerns the shared ground-truth label, so its value remains yes and N/M/K remains 20/14/5. A new native_action_translation annotation records that no source-defined translation maps every guard's native predicate to one catch event; reconstructed values are renamed as adapter-bit statistics.

What this census does not claim

  • It does not claim any evaluated stack performs poorly — an empty column is a reporting fact, not a performance finding.
  • It does not claim the unmeasured joint statistics would reveal dependence; measuring instead of assuming is the entire point.
  • Its 5 is an inclusive discovery count of noninterchangeable artifacts — not an all-miss rate, a stack-quality score, or a deployment conclusion.
  • It does not audit the quality of any per-system evaluation beyond the fields each row records.
  • It covers the artifacts found by the documented bounded search — not everything in existence. A qualifying artifact it missed falsifies the "among N" statement and is added on discovery.

The boundary of the search

Examined and excluded

unsafebench-2024

UnsafeBench: Benchmarking Image Safety Classifiers on Real-World and AI-Generated Images (Qu et al., CISPA — arXiv 2405.03486) — source ↗

Excluded: Fails frozen domain criterion 5: it evaluates image safety classifiers guarding image-generation platforms, not guardrails around LLM systems. Recorded loudly rather than quietly, because it is the strongest joint-statistic reporter the search found anywhere: Tables 5 and 12 print six OR-rule ensemble rows (four pairwise, one three-way, one five-way over the conventional classifiers, 'the image is unsafe if any classifier in the ensemble reports it'), as F1, with no all-miss or overlap decomposition. A census with a broader multimodal-moderation domain would count it PRESENT. This is also the artifact previously misremembered as "MSBench with two pairwise ensemble rows" — the acronym was wrong and the ensemble count is six, not two.

bells-framework-2024

BELLS: A Framework Towards Future Proof Benchmarks for the Evaluation of LLM Safeguards (arXiv 2406.01364) — source ↗

Excluded: Framework and position paper: reviews safeguards narratively and instantiates one MACHIAVELLI-based detector baseline, but contains no separately attributable multi-system evaluation — fails criteria 2 and 3. The empirical BELLS artifacts are separate rows above.

jailbreakbench

Excluded: Scores attack success against target LLMs with generic defenses — base-model robustness, not separately attributable guard systems.

The missing row, specified

The fix is small enough to paste into a results table: union detection and the all-miss rate over the same items, with the denominator and event definition that make them meaningful. The Minimum Joint Guardrail Disclosure page carries the exact template, its preconditions, and a tested reference implementation.

Corrections and revision history

Changes to this census are recorded here, in the page they change — not only in a repository log. Row-level corrections (8 recorded) live inside each row above. The canonical correction policy states the response and logging rules.

  • 2026-09-01 — Wayback precision. The pre-freeze-visibility-evidenced premise and the earlier entry of this date said checks on 2026-09-01 "found no web-archive capture"; the only archive queried was the Wayback Machine's CDX index, which held no capture of the repository at any date. archive.today and other archives were not queried. The premise now names the archive checked; the earlier entry stands as written rather than being silently reworded, per this record's correction rule. No row, classification, count, or sensitivity envelope changed.
  • 2026-09-01 — Date-evidence sensitivity declared for the 2026-08-30 addition. The row multimodal-safeguard-bench-2026 entered on GitHub-recorded dates (repository created 2026-06-02, pinned snapshot dated 2026-07-13); neither stamp records when the repository became publicly visible, and checks on 2026-09-01 found no web-archive capture of the repository at any date and no forks. That gap was prose in the 2026-08-30 entry; it is now the declared sensitivity pre-freeze-visibility-evidenced, whose alternative envelope is mechanically asserted: excluding the row yields N/M/K 19/13/4 and an M ladder of 13/12/0, while the ABSENT classification count stays 14 because the excluded row is PRESENT. The two headline 14s — the no-joint-artifact classification count and the shared-basis ladder rung — are different partitions of the same 20 examined rows, and only the second depends on this row. A statement from the row's author is the evidence that would settle the reading either way. No row, classification, evidence field, or primary count changed.
  • 2026-09-01 — Contact routes de-harvested. Nine rows printed 20 author email addresses verbatim in contact_route; census.yaml is served publicly as machine-readable text/yaml at a crawlable URL, which made those rows a scrapeable contact list. Addresses are now written in the [at]/[dot] form this file already used elsewhere, so a human can still route a correction while a harvester cannot lift the list. No evidential field, classification, count, or ladder value changed: N/M/K remain 20/14/5. Recorded here rather than as nine per-row corrections because nothing about any source's evidence was corrected — only how this file republishes third-party contact details. v0_row_lock re-minted.
  • 2026-08-31 — Action-layer clarification for multimodal-safeguard-bench-2026. A source check of src/msbench/pipeline.py established that the harness uses `blocked` items to suppress target generation. A fixed block-on-any OR therefore remains a valid counterfactual harness-action calculation on the pinned rows; it does not restore a source-defined shared-event safety or catch interpretation. N/M/K and the M ladder remain 20/14/5 and 14/12/0. This corrects this record's scope, not the authors' counts, their disclosed pairwise compositions, or any deployed route.
  • 2026-08-31 — Semantic-scope correction for multimodal-safeguard-bench-2026. The row's old same-event evidence incorrectly treated the harness's normalized `blocked` bit as the shared event. Under the frozen protocol, that field concerns the common HarmBench/XSTest ground-truth label and remains yes. A new native_action_translation annotation records that no source-defined map from all native guard predicates to one catch event was found. MC-004's counts are retained as adapter-bit arithmetic and no longer called a shared-event catch union; N/M/K and the M ladder remain 20/14/5 and 14/12/0. This corrects this record's semantic framing, not the authors' counts or their disclosed pairwise compositions.
  • 2026-08-31 — v0 frozen as a historical snapshot. Every examined row annotated with protocol-v1 vocabulary (source_type, reconstruction class, preservation state); v0_row_lock minted so history cannot change silently. Two classifications narrowed by the annotation: 14 marginals-only rows are recorded as PARTIALLY_IDENTIFIED rather than implying the joint is unknowable (comparable marginals bound it by sharp Frechet-Hoeffding limits), and circleguardbench-2025 is recorded as UNVERIFIED because its shared basis is unstated in the examined surfaces. No N/M/K value changed; no row was reclassified. Prospective collection rules for v1 were written and committed before the first v1 observation (census_protocol_v1.yaml).

The single number M was doing work it had not earned: the frozen criteria define "comparable" as shared items plus a shared event definition only, but a reader meets that word expecting matched operating thresholds and full exposure. compute_counts now derives an M ladder mechanically from fields already recorded on every row — 13 shared basis, 12 with no stated threshold mismatch (ML6 states the mismatch), 0 documenting matched thresholds with full exposure — and the page renders all three rungs. The proposition template gained an inline gloss saying which reading M uses. No row's evidence or classification changed; this is a weakening of what the headline implies, not a rescue of it.   • 2026-08-30 — Schema v3, prompted by a public self-contradiction rather than by any evidence error. The flagship page derived its headline K from compute_counts and, four paragraphs later, stated a hand-typed K of 4 in its non-claims list. Every gate passed: the census was internally coherent, the HTML matched its generator byte-for-byte, the deployed checksum matched, and the deployed smoke test asserted N and the M ladder but never K. The record's promise is that public claims stay bound to their evidence, so a page publicly stating two values for its own headline quantity is a release blocker and not a typo. Three changes follow. (1) Rows may declare joint_scope_additional, so a row carrying two kinds of joint evidence says so as data; the counts of artifacts that print a composition result, that release aligned per-item outcomes, and that do both are now derived by compute_counts instead of counted by hand in prose. No row's classification, evidence, or primary joint_scope changed, and N, M, K and the M ladder are unchanged at 20/14/5 and 14/12/0. (2) Every census quantity the site states now carries a stable identity, checked against this file on every push and against the served bytes after every deploy. (3) Historical counts must date themselves in markup; an undated superseded envelope now fails CI. This entry records a verification failure, not a measurement failure.

Correct this record

If a row misreads its source, a supposedly absent statistic exists, or a qualifying evaluation is missing: open an issue ↗ or write to bhavepranavwork@gmail.com. A confirmed correction updates the row, the counts, and this history — being corrected is the mechanism working, and correction credit is recorded in the row.

Benchmark authors: if you retained one decision per item per system, the minimum joint disclosure is one table away — and this census reclassifies your row to present the day you publish it.

Replay manifest

The exact commands that re-verify this census, starting from an empty directory: a POSIX shell with git and Python 3.11+ (with its standard venv module) is the whole environment. Nothing on this page requires trusting this page.

git clone https://github.com/Cubits11/cubits11.github.io.git
cd cubits11.github.io
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt       # pyyaml — the only dependency
python scripts/verify_census.py --counts        # row shape + N/M/K recomputed from census.yaml
python scripts/generate_missing_column.py --check  # this page matches the census file
python scripts/verify_figures.py                # figure geometry, asserted to 1e-9
python scripts/mjgd_reference.py --test         # the disclosure arithmetic, tested

Those four checks verify this census. The whole-repository replay — every claim binding, generated page, figure assertion, and bound reproduction, re-run from a fresh clone of one commit — is one further command from the same shell: python scripts/verify_clean_clone.py. The separately pinned MC-004 computation is reproducible from its released files.
